clue.text: Passion's audibly more macho in the East End

indicators.note: audibly tells us to go by how the words sound when spoken, not how they are spelt

parts.words: more macho in the East End
parts.note: more macho is harder, and a Cockney from London's East End drops the H, saying 'arder

explanation.surface: A remark that passion sounds tougher when spoken in a London accent.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End is the traditional Cockney part of London, where an initial H is famously dropped; non-rhotic 'arder then sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardour is a synonym for intense passion or enthusiasm.

clue.text: Cheap gold and diamonds in friendly environment

indicators.note: the friendly word forms an environment, a surrounding, for the gold and diamonds

parts.note: friendly means affable
OR is the heraldic word for gold
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: Jewellery that seems inexpensive because it is sold somewhere pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cheap is within one's means, i.e. reasonably priced.

clue.text: Head of Meteorology differs, first drawing line on her map

indicators.note: first says the word for differs comes before the other piece

parts.note: differs read as two words: is other

indicators.note: head of means take the opening letter of Meteorology

explanation.surface: A weather forecaster's chief disagrees about what to draw on the map.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'differs' as IS OTHER; 'drawing' is a link, and 'her' is the meteorologist whose map it is.
explanation.definitionFit: An isotherm is a contour joining places of equal temperature on a weather chart.

clue.text: A French parent adopting Portugal's current unit

indicators.note: adopting means the parent takes in the other piece, holding it inside

parts.note: mère is French for mother
P is the international vehicle code for Portugal

explanation.surface: A French mother adopts a child from Portugal.
explanation.definitionFit: The ampere is the SI unit for measuring electric current.

clue.text: A quiet river on location — just the job!

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction to play quietly
the Po is the main river of northern Italy
a site is a location

explanation.surface: A peaceful riverside spot that is perfect for the work.
explanation.definitionFit: Apposite means highly appropriate, exactly fitting the situation.

clue.text: Prince of the Stars embracing love of country

indicators.note: embracing means holding the other piece inside

parts.note: astral means of the stars
love is zero in tennis scoring, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A celestial prince who embraces patriotic love of his homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' is the countryside, not the nation the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastoral describes rural life, the countryside as opposed to town.

clue.text: Branch frequently receiving loud order to go away

indicators.note: receiving means the word for frequently takes the others inside

parts.note: oft is a poetic word for often
F is forte, the musical direction for loud
shoo is what one says to send an animal away

explanation.surface: A bough often gets shouted at to clear off.
explanation.definitionFit: An offshoot is a side shoot from a plant, or a subsidiary of an organisation.

clue.text: State beheaded Italian

indicators.note: beheaded means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a Roman is an Italian, from Rome

explanation.surface: A country executed an Italian by beheading.
explanation.definitionFit: Oman is a sovereign state on the Arabian Peninsula.

clue.text: Article on women's muscle

parts.note: the is the definite article
W is an abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: A magazine piece about female muscle.
explanation.definitionFit: Thew is an old word for muscular strength or a sinew.

clue.text: Reported drunk on machine part

indicators.note: reported signals that we hear the words, as if passed on by speech

parts.note: pissed is British slang for drunk, so drunk on is pissed on

explanation.surface: Someone said to be drunk on a piece of machinery.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang 'pissed' means drunk, not angry.
explanation.definitionFit: A piston is the sliding cylinder component inside an engine or pump.

clue.text: Snake given hint of annual contest

parts.note: a boa is a constricting snake
a trace is a slight hint or suggestion

explanation.surface: A serpent gets a clue about a yearly competition.
explanation.walkthrough: The Boat Race is the yearly Oxford v Cambridge rowing race on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oxford-Cambridge rowing race on the Thames is held every spring.

clue.text: Town in the Midlands turned around opening of televised game

indicators.note: around means the word for turned goes round the other letter

parts.note: milk that has turned has gone sour

indicators.note: opening of means the first letter of televised

parts.note: bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A Midlands town reversed its decision about a televised game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned around' looks like a reversal, but 'turned' is SOUR and 'around' puts it round T.
explanation.definitionFit: Stourbridge is a town in the West Midlands, known for glassmaking.

clue.text: Scientific theory of shared confidential knowledge not beginning to involve backstory

indicators.note: to involve means to take the other piece inside
not beginning means without its first letter

parts.note: privity is shared knowledge of something private
read as back story: a story is a tale, written backwards

explanation.surface: A theory built on secrets shared among insiders, with a history behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backstory' reads as one word, but it splits into 'back' (reverse) and 'story' (TALE), giving ELAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Einstein's theory of relativity is the famous physics theory of space and time.

clue.text: Poisoning slut, I melted into rising crowd

indicators.note: into means the rearranged letters go inside the other piece
rising in a down clue means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: a mob is a crowd

indicators.note: melted means the letters lose their shape and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lurid scene of a woman dissolving into a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Melted' is the anagram signal, 'rising' turns the crowd upwards since this is a down clue, and 'into' places the scrambled letters within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Botulism is a severe food poisoning caused by a bacterial toxin.

clue.text: Expose skull of aggressive youth?

parts.note: to skin something is to strip off its covering, exposing it
the skull is the head

explanation.surface: Revealing the skull of a violent young thug.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is by example: not every aggressive youth is one.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaven-headed youth subculture is often associated with violence.

clue.text: T-telling-off for being lachrymose

parts.note: an earful is a scolding, a telling-off

explanation.surface: A stammered reprimand leaves someone in tears.
explanation.walkthrough: The stammer 'T-' supplies the letter T itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Lachrymose means weeping or inclined to weep.

clue.text: Girly artist with sunny exterior

indicators.note: exterior means the word for sunny forms the outside of the artist

parts.note: fine weather is sunny weather
Tracey Emin is a British artist

explanation.surface: An artist with a cheerful outward manner who seems girlish.
explanation.walkthrough: Tracey Emin is the British artist known for My Bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Girly and feminine both describe qualities traditionally associated with women.

clue.text: Tramp's parody of Orcadian brew

parts.note: a bum is a vagrant, a tramp
a mock is an imitation or parody

explanation.surface: A vagrant's satire on a beer from Orkney.
explanation.walkthrough: Orcadian means from Orkney, the Scottish islands; bummock is a traditional ale brewed there at Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Bummock is a dialect name for a strong home-brewed Orkney ale.

clue.text: Gin or meths?

parts.note: ruined, the letters of mothers become or meths, so the answer read as wordplay produces these words

explanation.surface: A question of whether a spirit is gin or methylated spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: Mother's ruin is an old British nickname for gin. Read as wordplay, 'ruin' shuffles MOTHERS into 'or meths'.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional slang name for gin, from its ruinous effect on poor families.

clue.text: Drinks up, carrying home type of tap?

indicators.note: carrying means the reversed word holds the other piece inside
up in a down clue means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: an animal laps when it drinks
in means at home

explanation.surface: Drinking up while taking home a kind of tap.
explanation.walkthrough: A spinal tap is a lumbar puncture; the question mark flags that 'tap' is not a faucet.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinal tap draws fluid from the spinal canal for diagnosis.

clue.text: Plant playing card right

parts.note: an ace is a playing card

explanation.surface: Planting the correct playing card, as a cheat might.
explanation.definitionFit: Acer is the botanical genus of maples, a plant.

clue.text: Deity lives twice

indicators.note: twice means the word is written two times in a row

parts.note: lives means exists, which is to say is

explanation.surface: A god who has lived two lives.
explanation.definitionFit: Isis was the Egyptian goddess of motherhood and magic.

clue.text: Ladies' man's old hospital round interrupts drink

indicators.note: interrupts means breaking into the middle of the drink

parts.note: cava is Spanish sparkling wine
san is a dated short form of sanatorium
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A womaniser's old hospital rounds are interrupted by a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Giacomo Casanova was a famous Venetian seducer, now a byword for a womaniser.

clue.text: Look pleased about one figure of speech

indicators.note: about means the word for look pleased goes round the other piece

parts.note: to smile is to look pleased
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Being pleased about a single turn of phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' looks like a number, which 'one' supports, but it is a figure of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A simile is a rhetorical device comparing two things with like or as.

clue.text: Strike a chord with judge holding bouquet the wrong way round

indicators.note: holding means the word for judge contains the other piece

parts.note: to rate is to judge

indicators.note: the wrong way round means the word is written backwards

parts.note: a wine's nose is its bouquet

explanation.surface: Moving a judge by presenting flowers upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouquet' suggests flowers, but it is a wine's aroma, NOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To resonate is to evoke a response or feeling, the idiom strike a chord.

clue.text: Law curtailed lecture on dirt

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a talk is a lecture
mud is wet dirt

explanation.surface: A legal lecture cut short to dish the dirt.
explanation.definitionFit: The Talmud is the body of Jewish civil and ceremonial law and commentary.
